ja: だいにじゅうはちかい

p.src: Now Guan Yu, accompanied by Sun Qian, was escorting his two sisters-in-law toward Runan when, unexpectedly, Xiahou Dun came pursuing from behind with more than two hundred horsemen. Sun Qian went on ahead, guarding the carriages and baggage. Guan Yu turned back, reined in his horse, and, resting a hand upon his blade, demanded, “By pursuing me, you do your Chancellor’s magnanimity a disservice.” Xiahou Dun replied, “The Chancellor sent no written order to inform us. You have killed men along the road and even slain one of my officers. Your insolence has gone too far! I have come expressly to seize you and deliver you to the Chancellor for judgment!”

p.src: With that, he spurred his horse and leveled his spear to fight. Just then a lone rider came galloping from behind, shouting, “You must not fight Yun-chang!” Guan Yu held his reins and remained still. The messenger drew an official document from his robe and said to Xiahou Dun, “The Chancellor esteems General Guan’s loyalty and righteousness. Fearing that he might be stopped at the passes along the road, he sent me with this document to circulate everywhere.” Xiahou Dun said, “Does the Chancellor know that Guan killed the officers and soldiers guarding the passes along the way?” The messenger replied, “That he does not yet know.” Xiahou Dun said, “I shall merely take him alive before the Chancellor and let the Chancellor himself release him.” Guan Yu cried angrily, “Do you think I fear you?” He spurred his horse, raised his blade, and charged straight at Xiahou Dun.

p.src: Xiahou Dun advanced with his spear to meet him. Their horses met, and before they had exchanged ten bouts, another rider suddenly galloped up, shouting, “Generals, cease fighting a moment!” Xiahou Dun lowered his spear and asked the messenger, “Has the Chancellor ordered Guan’s capture?” The messenger answered, “No. The Chancellor feared that the generals guarding the passes might obstruct General Guan, so he sent me racing here with another document ordering that he be allowed through.” Xiahou Dun asked, “Does the Chancellor know he has killed men along the road?” The messenger replied, “He does not.” Xiahou Dun said, “Since he does not know of the killings, Guan cannot be allowed to leave.” He ordered his soldiers to surround Guan Yu. Guan Yu flew into a rage and brandished his blade to meet them.

p.src: Just as the two were about to clash, a man galloped up from behind the ranks and shouted, “Yun-chang! Yuan-rang! Do not fight!” All looked and saw that it was Zhang Liao. Both men reined in their horses. Zhang Liao came forward and said, “I bear the Chancellor’s command. Having learned that Yun-chang slew the guards and generals at the passes, he feared that obstacles might arise along the road. He therefore sent me expressly to notify every pass that he is to be allowed through unhindered.” Xiahou Dun said, “Qin Qi was Cai Yang’s nephew. Cai Yang entrusted Qin Qi to my care. Now that Guan has killed him, how can I possibly let the matter rest?” Zhang Liao said, “When I see General Cai, I shall explain the matter myself. Since the Chancellor, in his magnanimity, has ordered that Yun-chang be allowed to go, none of you may thwart his will.” Xiahou Dun had no choice but to order his troops to withdraw. Zhang Liao asked, “Where do you mean to go now, Yun-chang?” Guan Yu replied, “I hear that my elder brother is no longer with Yuan Shao. I shall now search the whole realm for him.” Zhang Liao said, “Since Xuande’s whereabouts remain unknown, why not return for the time being and see the Chancellor again?” Guan Yu laughed. “How could there be any sense in that! Wenyuan, when you return to the Chancellor, kindly apologize to him on my behalf.” Having said this, he exchanged a clasped-hands salute with Zhang Liao and took his leave.

p.src: Zhang Liao and Xiahou Dun then led their troops back. Guan Yu caught up with the carriages and told Sun Qian what had happened. The two rode onward side by side. After several days’ travel, they were suddenly caught in a torrential rain, and all their baggage was soaked. In the distance they saw a manor beside a hill. Guan Yu led the carriages there and asked for lodging. An old man came out of the manor to welcome them. Guan Yu explained fully why they had come. The old man said, “My surname is Guo and my given name is Chang. My family has lived here for generations. I have long heard of your great name and count myself fortunate to behold you and pay my respects.” He had a sheep slaughtered and wine prepared for their entertainment, and invited the two ladies to rest in the rear hall. Guo Chang accompanied Guan Yu and Sun Qian as they drank in the thatched hall. Meanwhile, the baggage was dried by the fire and the horses were fed.

p.src: At dusk, a young man suddenly appeared, leading several others into the manor, and went straight up to the thatched hall. Guo Chang called out, “My son, come and pay your respects to the general.” Then he said to Guan Yu, “This is my foolish son.” Guan Yu asked where he had been. Guo Chang replied, “He has just returned from hunting.” After paying his respects to Guan Yu, the young man left the hall. Guo Chang said tearfully, “This old man’s family has always made its living through farming and study. I have only this one son, yet he neglects our proper calling and occupies himself solely with roaming and hunting. It is a misfortune to our house!” Guan Yu said, “In these troubled times, if he masters the martial arts, he may yet win rank and renown. Why call it a misfortune?” Guo Chang replied, “If he were willing to learn the martial arts, he would indeed be a young man of ambition; but now he devotes himself entirely to idleness and dissipation, stopping at no mischief. That is why this old man grieves!”

p.src: Guan Yu too sighed at this. Late in the night, Guo Chang took his leave and withdrew. Just as Guan Yu and Sun Qian were about to retire, they suddenly heard horses neighing and men shouting in the rear courtyard. Guan Yu hurriedly called his attendants, but none answered, so he and Sun Qian took up their swords and went to investigate. There they saw Guo Chang’s son lying on the ground and crying out, while Guan Yu’s attendants were fighting with the manor servants. Guan Yu asked what had happened. An attendant replied, “This man came to steal the Red Hare, but the horse kicked him down. We heard the commotion and rose to inspect the place, but the manor servants came and started brawling with us.” Guan Yu cried angrily, “How dare this petty thief steal my horse!”

p.src: Just as he was about to punish him, Guo Chang rushed up and pleaded, “My unworthy son has committed this wicked deed and deserves ten thousand deaths! But my old wife dotes upon him above all else. I beg you, General, to show mercy and forgive him!” Guan Yu said, “Your son is indeed unworthy. What you said earlier proves that no one knows a son better than his father. Out of regard for you, I shall spare him for now.” He then ordered his attendants to guard the horses carefully, dispersed the manor servants with a shout, and returned with Sun Qian to rest in the thatched hall. The next day, Guo Chang and his wife came before the hall and bowed, saying, “Our wretched son offended your formidable dignity. We are deeply grateful for the mercy with which you forgave him.” Guan Yu said, “Call him out, and I shall set him right with some honest counsel.” Guo Chang replied, “During the fourth watch he again gathered several ruffians and went off somewhere. I do not know where.”

p.src: Guan Yu thanked Guo Chang and bade him farewell, helped his two sisters-in-law into their carriage, and left the manor. Riding abreast with Sun Qian, he guarded the carriages as they followed a mountain road. Before they had gone thirty li, more than a hundred men suddenly poured out from behind a mountain, led by two horsemen. The man in front wore a yellow scarf around his head and a battle robe upon his body; the man behind was Guo Chang’s son. The man in the yellow scarf cried, “I was a subordinate general of Zhang Jue, General of Heaven! You who approach, leave the Red Hare at once, and I shall let you pass!” Guan Yu laughed loudly. “You ignorant, reckless brigand! Since you followed Zhang Jue in banditry, do you know the names of the three sworn brothers Liu, Guan, and Zhang?” The man in the yellow scarf replied, “I have only heard that the red-faced man with the long beard is named Guan Yun-chang, but I have never seen his face. Who are you?”

p.src: Guan Yu halted his horse and rested his blade, untied his beard bag, and drew out his long beard for the man to see. The man tumbled from his saddle, seized Guo Chang’s son by the hair, and presented him on his knees before Guan Yu’s horse. Guan Yu asked his name. He replied, “My surname is Pei, and my given name is Yuanshao. Ever since Zhang Jue died, I have had no master. I gathered a band in the mountains and forests and have been hiding here for the time being. This scoundrel came this morning and reported, ‘A traveler riding a thousand-li horse has lodged at my home.’ He invited me expressly to come and seize the horse. I never imagined that I would encounter you, General.” Guo Chang’s son prostrated himself and begged for his life. Guan Yu said, “Out of regard for your father, I shall spare your life!”

p.src: Guo fled in abject terror, clutching his head. Lord Guan asked Pei Yuanshao, “You did not recognize my face, so how did you know my name?” Yuanshao replied, “Twenty li from here stands a place called Crouching Ox Mountain. On that mountain is a man from west of the passes, surnamed Zhou and named Cang, whose two arms possess the strength of a thousand jin. He has broad, ridged ribs and a curling beard, and is a most imposing figure. He was formerly an officer under Zhang Bao of the Yellow Turbans, but after Zhang Bao died, he gathered a band in the mountains and forests. He has often spoken to me of your great renown, General, and lamented that he had no means of meeting you.” Lord Guan said, “The greenwood is no place for men of valor to make their home. From this day onward, each of you should forsake evil and return to the right path; do not bring ruin upon yourselves.” Yuanshao bowed and thanked him.

p.src: While they were still speaking, they saw in the distance a troop of horsemen approaching. Yuanshao said, “That must be Zhou Cang.” Lord Guan reined in his horse and waited. Sure enough, a tall, dark-faced man appeared, riding with a spear in hand and leading a band of followers. On seeing Lord Guan, he exclaimed in astonished delight, “It is General Guan!” He hurriedly dismounted, bowed low, and prostrated himself by the roadside, saying, “Zhou Cang pays his respects.” Lord Guan asked, “Where did you ever come to know me, brave sir?” Cang replied, “When I formerly followed Zhang Bao of the Yellow Turbans, I once beheld your honored countenance. I bitterly regretted having fallen among bandits and being unable to follow you. Today, by good fortune, I have been granted an audience with you. If you will not disdain me, General, take me as a common foot soldier. Let me attend your stirrup and bear your whip from dawn to dusk, and I shall be content even to die!” Seeing that he was utterly sincere, Lord Guan asked, “If you follow me, what is to become of the men under your command?” Cang replied, “Those who wish to follow may all come with us; those who do not may do as they please.”

p.src: At this, all the men declared, “We wish to follow.” Lord Guan dismounted, went to the carriage, and sought the counsel of his two sisters-in-law. Lady Gan said, “Brother-in-law, since leaving the capital Xu, you have traveled alone all this way and endured countless hardships, yet never once sought an armed escort. When Liao Hua earlier wished to join you, you turned him away. Why, then, should Zhou Cang’s entire band alone be admitted now? We are only women of limited understanding; you must weigh the matter yourself.” Lord Guan said, “What you say, sister-in-law, is right.” He then told Zhou Cang, “It is not that I am unfeeling, but the two ladies do not consent. For now, return to the mountain. Once I have found my elder brother, I shall certainly come and summon you.” Zhou Cang kowtowed and pleaded, “I am but a rough and reckless fellow who fell into banditry. Now that I have encountered you, General, it is as though I have seen the light of heaven once more. How could I bear to let this chance pass again? If it is inconvenient for all these men to accompany you, they may all be ordered to follow Pei Yuanshao. I alone shall follow you on foot, General, and would not shrink even from a journey of ten thousand li!” Lord Guan relayed these words to his two sisters-in-law. Lady Gan said, “One or two men accompanying us will cause no difficulty.” Lord Guan then ordered Zhou Cang to assign the men to accompany Pei Yuanshao. Yuanshao said, “I too wish to follow General Guan.” Zhou Cang replied, “If you go as well, all the men will scatter. For the time being, take command of them. I shall go with General Guan, and as soon as we have found a settled place, I will come back for you.”

p.src: Yuanshao parted from them in dejection. Zhou Cang followed Lord Guan as they set out toward Runan. After traveling for several days, they saw a walled town in the distance. Lord Guan asked a local, “What place is this?” The local replied, “This place is called Gucheng. Several months ago, a general surnamed Zhang and named Fei arrived here with several dozen horsemen, drove out the county magistrate, occupied Gucheng, recruited soldiers, purchased horses, gathered fodder, and stored provisions. He now has three to five thousand troops assembled, and no one for miles around dares oppose him.” Lord Guan rejoiced. “Since my brother and I were separated at Xuzhou, I have known nothing of his whereabouts. Who would have thought he was here!” He ordered Sun Qian to enter the town first and announce their arrival, telling Zhang Fei to come and welcome his two sisters-in-law. Now Zhang Fei had stayed on Mount Mangdang for over a month. When he went out to seek news of Xuande, he happened to pass Gucheng and entered the county seat to request provisions. When the magistrate refused, Zhang Fei flew into a rage, drove him out, seized the county seal, occupied the town, and settled there for the time being. That day, bearing Lord Guan’s instructions, Sun Qian entered the town and met Zhang Fei. After exchanging courtesies, he gave a full account: “Xuande has left Yuan Shao and gone to Runan. Now Yunchang has escorted the two ladies here all the way from the capital Xu and asks you, General, to come out and receive them.”

p.src: When Zhang Fei had heard him out, he answered not a word. He immediately donned his armor, took up his eighteen-foot spear, mounted his horse, and led over a thousand men straight out through the north gate. Sun Qian was astonished but dared not ask what was happening, and could only follow him out of the town. When Lord Guan saw Zhang Fei approaching, he was beside himself with joy. He handed his blade to Zhou Cang, spurred his horse, and rode forward to meet him. But Zhang Fei’s great round eyes were glaring, his tiger whiskers bristled upward, and with a roar like thunder he brandished his spear and thrust straight at Lord Guan. Lord Guan was greatly startled and hastily dodged aside, crying, “Worthy brother, why are you acting like this? Have you forgotten our oath in the Peach Garden?” Zhang Fei shouted, “Having betrayed your honor, how dare you show your face before me!” Lord Guan said, “How have I betrayed my honor?” Zhang Fei replied, “You turned your back on our elder brother, surrendered to Cao Cao, and accepted a marquisate and noble rank. Now you have come to ensnare me as well! Today you and I shall fight to the death!” Lord Guan said, “So you know nothing of what happened. It is difficult for me to explain. Our two sisters-in-law are here before you; ask them yourself, worthy brother.”

Lord Guan was greatly startled and hastily dodged aside, crying, “Worthy brother, why are you acting like this?
Have you forgotten our oath in the Peach Garden?”
Zhang Fei shouted, “Having betrayed your honor, how dare you show your face before me!”
Lord Guan said, “How have I betrayed my honor?”
Zhang Fei replied, “You turned your back on our elder brother, surrendered to Cao Cao, and accepted a marquisate and noble rank.
Now you have come to ensnare me as well!
Today you and I shall fight to the death!”
Lord Guan said, “So you know nothing of what happened. It is difficult for me to explain.
Our two sisters-in-law are here before you; ask them yourself, worthy brother.”

p.src: Hearing this, the two ladies raised the carriage curtain and called out, “Third brother, why are you behaving like this?” Zhang Fei said, “Stay where you are, sisters-in-law. First watch me kill this faithless man; afterward I shall invite you into the town.” Lady Gan said, “Your second brother did not know what had become of any of you, and therefore took temporary refuge with the Cao clan. Now that he knows your elder brother is in Runan, he has braved every danger and hardship expressly to escort us here. Third brother, do not misjudge him.” Lady Mi said, “Your second brother’s stay in the capital Xu was forced upon him by necessity.” Zhang Fei said, “Sisters-in-law, do not let him deceive you! A loyal subject would rather die than suffer disgrace. How could a true man ever serve two masters?” Lord Guan said, “Worthy brother, do not wrong me.” Sun Qian said, “Yunchang came here expressly to seek you, General.” Zhang Fei shouted, “How can you talk such nonsense too? He harbors no good intentions! He must have come to capture me!” Lord Guan said, “If I had come to capture you, I would surely have brought troops with me.” Zhang Fei pointed and cried, “Then what are those if not troops coming this way?”

p.src: Presently, Cao Cao’s troops arrived. Their leading commander was Cai Yang. Brandishing his saber and spurring his horse, he shouted, “You killed my nephew Qin Qi, and here you are hiding! By the prime minister’s command, I have come expressly to seize you!” Lord Guan wasted no words, but raised his blade and struck. Zhang Fei beat the drum with his own hands. Before the first roll had even ended, Lord Guan’s blade flashed, and Cai Yang’s head had already fallen to the ground. All the soldiers fled. Lord Guan captured alive the young soldier who bore the identification banner and brought him forward to ask what had happened. The soldier explained, “When Cai Yang heard that you had killed his nephew, General, he became furious and wished to come to Hebei to fight you. The prime minister would not permit it, and instead sent him to Runan to attack Liu Pi. He never expected to encounter you here, General.” On hearing this, Lord Guan ordered the soldier to go before Zhang Fei and relate the matter. Zhang Fei questioned the soldier closely about Lord Guan’s affairs while he was in the capital Xu. The soldier recounted everything from beginning to end, and only then did Zhang Fei believe him.

p.src: As they were speaking, a soldier suddenly came from the city to report, “More than ten horsemen are approaching the south gate at great speed. We do not know who they are.” Zhang Fei grew suspicious and rode out through the south gate to look. Sure enough, more than ten lightly armed horsemen carrying small bows and short arrows were approaching. At the sight of Zhang Fei, they tumbled from their saddles and dismounted. Looking closely, he saw that they were Mi Zhu and Mi Fang. Zhang Fei also dismounted to greet them. Mi Zhu said, “After we were separated at Xuzhou, my brother and I fled the turmoil and returned home. We sent men far and wide to seek news and learned that Yun-chang had submitted to Cao Cao, while our lord was in Hebei. We also heard that Jian Yong had gone to join him in Hebei. Only your whereabouts were unknown to us. Yesterday on the road we met a band of travelers who said that a general surnamed Zhang, matching your appearance, now held the Old City. My brother and I reckoned that it must be you, so we came in search of you. How fortunate that we have found you!” Zhang Fei said, “Brother Yun-chang and Sun Qian have just arrived escorting my two sisters-in-law, and we already know where our elder brother is.”

p.src: The next day, Zhang Fei wished to accompany Lord Guan to Runan to see Xuande. Lord Guan said, “Worthy brother, remain in this city for now and protect our two sisters-in-law. Sun Qian and I will go first to seek news of our elder brother.” Zhang Fei agreed. Lord Guan and Sun Qian set out for Runan with several horsemen. Liu Pi and Gong Du received them, and Lord Guan immediately asked, “Where is the Imperial Uncle?” Liu Pi replied, “The Imperial Uncle stayed here for several days, but seeing that our forces were too few, he returned to Yuan Benchu in Hebei to confer with him.” Lord Guan was bitterly disappointed. Sun Qian said, “There is no need to worry. Let us endure one more hard journey, return to Hebei, inform the Imperial Uncle, and then all go together to the Old City.”

Lord Guan said, “This city gives us a place of refuge and must not be lightly abandoned. I will go again with Sun Qian to Yuan Shao, find our elder brother, and bring him here to reunite with us. Worthy brother, you must hold this city securely.” Zhang Fei said, “Brother, after slaying his Yan Liang and Wen Chou, how can you possibly go there?” Lord Guan said, “It does not matter. Once there, I shall act as circumstances require.” He then summoned Zhou Cang and asked, “How many men and horses are there with Pei Yuanshao at Crouching Ox Mountain?” Zhou Cang replied, “About four or five hundred.” Lord Guan said, “I shall now take a shortcut to seek our elder brother. Go to Crouching Ox Mountain, muster that band, and bring them by the main road to meet us.”

p.src: Zhou Cang accepted the order and departed. Lord Guan and Sun Qian set out for Hebei with only a little over twenty horsemen. As they neared the border, Sun Qian said, “General, you must not enter rashly. Rest here for the time being. Let me go in first to see the Imperial Uncle, and then we can make further plans.” Lord Guan followed his advice and sent Sun Qian on ahead. Seeing a manor in a village in the distance, he and his attendants went there to seek lodging. An old man came out of the manor leaning on a staff and saluted Lord Guan. Lord Guan told him the full truth. The old man said, “My surname is also Guan, and my given name is Ding. I have long heard of your great name and am fortunate to behold you today.” He then summoned his two sons to meet Lord Guan and cordially lodged him and all his attendants at the manor.

Jian Yong said, “Tomorrow, my lord, tell Yuan Shao that you wish to go to Jingzhou and persuade Liu Biao to join in destroying Cao Cao. You can then seize the opportunity to leave.” Xuande said, “An excellent plan! But can you accompany me?” Jian Yong replied, “I have my own plan for getting away.”

p.src: Their plans were settled. The next day Xuande went to see Yuan Shao and said, “Liu Jingsheng commands the nine commanderies of Jing and Xiang. His troops are excellent and his provisions abundant. You should make an alliance with him and attack Cao Cao together.” Yuan Shao said, “I once sent an envoy to propose an alliance, but he refused to comply.” Xuande said, “He and I are of the same clan. If I go to persuade him, he will certainly not refuse.” Yuan Shao said, “Winning Liu Biao would be far better than winning Liu Pi.” He accordingly ordered Xuande to go. Yuan Shao added, “I recently heard that Guan Yun-chang has left Cao Cao and intends to come to Hebei. I shall kill him to avenge Yan Liang and Wen Chou!” Xuande said, “Your Excellency previously wished to employ him, and that is why I summoned him. Why do you now wish to kill him? Yan Liang and Wen Chou were but two deer beside him; Yun-chang is a tiger. Having lost two deer and gained a tiger, what cause is there for resentment?” Yuan Shao laughed and said, “Of course I cherish him. I was only speaking in jest. Send someone again to summon him and tell him to come quickly.” Xuande said, “Then Sun Qian can be sent to summon him.” Yuan Shao was delighted and agreed.

p.src: Now Xuande first ordered Sun Qian to leave the city and report the news to Lord Guan. Meanwhile, he and Jian Yong took leave of Yuan Shao, mounted their horses, and rode out of the city. When they reached the border, Sun Qian met them, and together they proceeded to Guan Ding’s manor. Lord Guan came to the gate to receive him with bows. They clasped hands and wept without cease. Guan Ding led his two sons in bowing before them outside the thatched hall. Xuande asked their names. Lord Guan said, “This man bears the same surname as I do and has two sons. His elder son, Guan Ning, studies letters. His younger son, Guan Ping, studies the martial arts.” Guan Ding said, “I would now like to send my younger son to follow General Guan, but I do not know whether you would be willing to accept him.” Xuande asked, “How old is he?” Guan Ding replied, “He is eighteen.” Xuande said, “Since you show us such kindness, and my brother still has no son, what if he were to take your worthy son as his own?” Guan Ding was overjoyed and at once ordered Guan Ping to bow to Lord Guan as his father and address Xuande as his uncle. Fearing that Yuan Shao might pursue them, Xuande hurriedly made ready to depart. Guan Ping followed Lord Guan, and they all set out together. Guan Ding accompanied them for part of the way and then returned home. Lord Guan directed them toward Crouching Ox Mountain.

p.src: As they traveled, they suddenly saw Zhou Cang approaching with several dozen wounded men. Lord Guan brought him before Xuande. Asked how he had been wounded, Zhou Cang replied, “Before I reached Crouching Ox Mountain, a lone general arrived on horseback and fought Pei Yuanshao. In a single bout he speared Pei Yuanshao to death, induced all his followers to surrender, and occupied the mountain stronghold. When I arrived and called upon the men to join me, only these few came over. All the rest were afraid and dared not leave without permission. Unable to endure the insult, I fought that general, but he defeated me several times in succession, and I received three spear wounds. Therefore I have come to report to my lord.” Xuande asked, “What did this man look like? What are his surname and given name?” Zhou Cang replied, “He was exceedingly mighty and robust, but I do not know his name.”

p.src: Thereupon Lord Guan spurred his horse into the lead, with Xuande behind him, and they made straight for Sleeping Ox Mountain. Zhou Cang was shouting challenges below the mountain when he saw the general, fully armed, charge down on horseback with spear in hand, leading his men. Xuande at once rode forward, brandished his whip, and cried, “Can the man approaching be none other than Zilong?” When the general saw Xuande, he tumbled from his saddle, dismounted, and prostrated himself beside the road. It was indeed Zhao Zilong. Xuande and Lord Guan both dismounted to greet him and asked how he had come to be there. Zhao Yun said, “Since I parted from you, my lord, Gongsun Zan, heedless of all counsel, suffered defeat and burned himself to death. Yuan Shao repeatedly invited me to join him. But I judged that he too was no man to employ talent wisely, and so I did not go. Later I intended to go to Xuzhou and enter your service, but then I heard that Xuzhou had fallen, that Yunchang had joined Cao Cao, and that you, my lord, were with Yuan Shao. Several times I wished to come and join you, but feared Yuan Shao would take offense. I wandered homeless throughout the realm, with nowhere to take refuge. Some time ago, while passing this place by chance, I happened upon Pei Yuanshao, who came down the mountain to seize my horse. I killed him and have taken shelter here ever since. Recently I heard that Yide was in the Ancient City and meant to seek him out, though I did not know whether the report was true. How fortunate that I have met you today, my lord!”

Xuande saw his brothers reunited, his officers and commanders all present, and Zhao Yun newly joined to him; Lord Guan, too, had gained Guan Ping and Zhou Cang. His joy knew no bounds, and they drank for several days in succession.
A later poet composed verses in praise of this:

p.src: At this time Xuande, Guan Yu, Zhang Fei, Zhao Yun, Sun Qian, Jian Yong, Mi Zhu, Mi Fang, Guan Ping, and Zhou Cang commanded altogether four or five thousand cavalrymen, infantrymen, officers, and soldiers. Xuande wished to abandon the Ancient City and take up the defense of Runan; just then Liu Pi and Gong Du sent messengers to invite him there. Thereupon he led his army to Runan and encamped there, recruiting soldiers and purchasing horses while gradually planning further campaigns. Of this no more need be said.

p.src: Now Yuan Shao, seeing that Xuande did not return, flew into a rage and wished to raise an army against him. Guo Tu said, “Liu Bei is not worth troubling over. Cao Cao is the formidable enemy and must be eliminated. Though Liu Biao holds Jingzhou, he is not strong enough to concern us. Sun Bofu of Jiangdong overawes the Three Rivers with his might; his lands extend across six commanderies, and he has many strategists and warriors. We should send someone to form an alliance with him and attack Cao Cao together.” Yuan Shao followed his advice, wrote a letter at once, and dispatched Chen Zhen as his envoy to meet Sun Ce. Indeed:
